script.base: Books have San Francisco laying 12.5 with a 28.5 implied total against a Miami team implied at 16.0, so the base flow is SF in front by halftime and leaning run after the lead. Week-1 SF rush pie was 30 carries: Kaelon Black 14/65 (46.7%), Christian McCaffrey 10/68 (33.3%, 6.8 YPC), Brock Purdy 5/29, Deebo Samuel 1/12. Miami's week-1 rush pie was only 18 carries: De'Von Achane 11/36 (61.1%, 3.27 YPC), Malik Willis 6/39, Jaylen Wright 1/-1. Once Miami trails, that already-small rush pie shrinks further and the 27 week-1 targets (Malik Washington 8, Caleb Douglas 7, Achane 5) become the offense. Pace slows late for SF; this is a clock-kill, not a 44.5 shootout, unless garbage-time Miami passes inflate the total without points.
script.flip1: Miami hangs around. Willis already had 6 designed rushes for 39 yards, and SF's run defense allowed 4.39 YPC with 2 runs of 10+, so a close game into the fourth keeps Achane near 11 carries and kills a 36.5 rush under. SF then cannot just hand the ball off, and McCaffrey's carry bump never arrives.
script.flip2: Black (groin, Questionable, not Out) is a full go and repeats 14 clock carries. SF can still lead 28-16 while McCaffrey stays on 10 carries and 68 rush yards, losing 68.5. The other kill is a 17-plus lead that benches both SF backs before the carry bump cashes.
